newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea 3-yr yields end higher on heavy new issues.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea 3-yr yields end higher on heavy new issues.

text.p: Yields on three-year corporates closed higher on Friday in thin trading as heavy new issues, estimated at 255 billion won, dampened buying sentiment, brokers said.

Three-month CD yields rose in line with a bearish tone in the longer-term bond trading. The overnight call rate fell as banks looked well prepared to meet the central bank's reserve requirements on Monday.
* 3-yr corporates end at 12.55 pct from 12.50 on Thursday
* 3-mth CDs close at 13.25 pct from 13.13 pct
Yields on three-year corporate bonds closed higher on Friday in thin trading as heavy new issues, estimated at 255 billion won, depressed sentiment, brokers said.
"There were a lot of new issues today and there will be more on Monday. That depressed trading," said a Daishin Securities broker. Brokers said new issues on Monday would exceed 300 billion won.
Three-month CD yields also rose in line with a bearish tone in the longer-term bond trading.
The overnight call rate fell as banks looked well prepared to meet the central bank's reserve requirements on Monday.
The release of 600 billion won from the state budget earlier this week also helped bring down the call rate.
